list.title: Computer Science
list.description: Learn the latest technologies and build skills for a successful tech career.
list.overview: The B.Sc. in Computer Science program gives you a strong base in programming, algorithms, databases and software development. Classroom theory is combined with coding labs so you can build applications, websites and problem-solving skills for the tech industry.
list.quote: Gain the skills, knowledge and confidence to shape a smarter, more connected tomorrow through the power of technology.

highlights.title: Programming First
highlights.desc: C, Java, Python and web fundamentals from year one

highlights.title: Coding Labs
highlights.desc: Weekly labs, hackathons and mini software projects

highlights.title: Industry Mentors
highlights.desc: Guidance from software engineers and IT faculty

highlights.title: Tech Placements
highlights.desc: Support for internships in IT firms and startups

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Programming Fundamentals
curriculum.content: Programming fundamentals, computer organization, discrete mathematics, English communication and an introduction to databases. Lab work includes writing basic programs, using office tools and understanding hardware components.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Data Structures & Web
curriculum.content: Data structures, object-oriented programming, operating systems, DBMS and web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript). You will build a small website, write SQL queries and complete coding assignments every semester.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Software Projects & Internship
curriculum.content: Software engineering, computer networks, Python applications, elective modules such as AI basics or cybersecurity, internship and a major capstone project presented to faculty and industry guests.

list.eligibility_text: This program is for students who enjoy computers, logic and building things with code. You can apply after 12th from any stream, though mathematics in 10+2 is an advantage.
list.career_text: Computer Science graduates work in software companies, IT services, product startups, banks and government e-governance projects. Many also pursue MCA, M.Sc. Computer Science or professional certifications in cloud and data.

faqs.question: Do I need PCM in 12th?
faqs.answer: PCM is helpful but not mandatory. Any-stream students with interest in coding can apply.

faqs.question: Will I learn practical coding?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every semester includes programming labs, mini-projects and a final-year capstone.

faqs.question: What is the duration and campus?
faqs.answer: 3 years, full time on campus at Main Campus, New Delhi.

eligibility_points: 12th pass from a recognized board (any stream).
Minimum 50% aggregate in the qualifying exam.
Mathematics in 10+2 is preferred, not compulsory.
Personal interview / counselling before final admission.

list.title: Business Administration
list.description: Develop leadership and management skills for a global career.
list.overview: The BBA program trains you in management, marketing, finance, HR and entrepreneurship. You study real company cases, make presentations and learn how businesses plan, sell, hire and grow in Indian and global markets.
list.quote: Learn to lead teams, take decisions and build businesses that create real impact.

highlights.title: Management Core
highlights.desc: Marketing, finance, HR and operations in one degree

highlights.title: Case Method
highlights.desc: Live business cases, role plays and presentations

highlights.title: Corporate Talks
highlights.desc: Sessions with managers, founders and alumni

highlights.title: Internship Track
highlights.desc: Summer internship in sales, HR or finance

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Business Basics
curriculum.content: Principles of management, business communication, microeconomics, accounting basics and business mathematics. You will prepare presentations, group discussions and a short market survey project.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Marketing, HR & Finance
curriculum.content: Marketing management, organizational behaviour, financial management, business law and HR practices. Case studies from Indian companies and a retail / digital marketing mini-project are part of this year.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Strategy, Startup & Internship
curriculum.content: Strategic management, entrepreneurship, elective in finance or marketing, internship and a business plan project. Placement workshops cover aptitude, GD and interviews.

list.eligibility_text: BBA is designed for students who want a career in management, startups or family business. You can join after 12th from commerce, science or arts.
list.career_text: BBA graduates join sales, marketing, HR, banking, operations and startup roles. Many go for MBA, professional courses like CA/CS support roles, or start their own venture.

faqs.question: Is commerce compulsory in 12th?
faqs.answer: No. Students from any stream can apply for BBA.

faqs.question: Is there an internship?
faqs.answer: Yes. A summer internship is part of the third-year learning plan.

faqs.question: What is the program duration?
faqs.answer: 3 years, full time, on campus.

eligibility_points: 12th pass (Commerce / Science / Arts) from a recognized board.
Minimum 50% marks in 10+2.
Good communication skills are an advantage.
Admission through merit list and counselling.

list.title: Arts & Humanities
list.description: Explore your creativity and build a strong foundation in humanities.
list.overview: The B.A. in Arts & Humanities explores literature, history, sociology, political science and creative writing. You learn to research, debate, write clearly and understand culture, society and media.
list.quote: Turn curiosity into insight and creativity into a career that inspires people and communities.

highlights.title: Liberal Arts Core
highlights.desc: Literature, history, sociology and political thought

highlights.title: Writing Studio
highlights.desc: Essays, reports, content writing and research papers

highlights.title: Seminars
highlights.desc: Debates, cultural events and guest lectures

highlights.title: Media Exposure
highlights.desc: Internships in publishing, NGOs and content teams

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Literature & History
curriculum.content: English literature, world history, introduction to sociology, environmental studies and academic writing. Tutorials focus on reading, note-making and spoken English.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Society, Politics & Media
curriculum.content: Indian society, political science, optional language, media studies basics and research methods. You will write term papers and take part in a departmental seminar.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Electives, Dissertation & Internship
curriculum.content: Electives such as journalism, public administration or gender studies, dissertation / project, internship with an NGO, school, media house or cultural organisation.

list.eligibility_text: This program suits students who enjoy reading, writing, history, society and languages. Arts, commerce or science students after 12th can apply.
list.career_text: Humanities graduates work in education, civil services preparation, journalism, content, publishing, NGOs, museums and public policy. Many continue with M.A., B.Ed., law or journalism diplomas.

faqs.question: Which subjects will I study?
faqs.answer: Literature, history, sociology, political science and writing, with later electives.

faqs.question: Can science students apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. The program is open after 12th from any stream.

faqs.question: Is there a research project?
faqs.answer: Yes. Final year includes a dissertation or field project.

eligibility_points: 12th pass from any stream with a recognized board.
Minimum 45–50% marks as per admission policy.
Interest in reading, writing and current affairs is expected.
Counselling round to understand your subject preference.

list.title: Engineering
list.description: Gain hands-on experience with modern tools and technologies.
list.overview: The B.Tech Engineering program covers core engineering science, workshop practice, CAD, electronics or mechanical fundamentals (as per branch intake) and industry projects. Emphasis is on labs, design thinking and safety standards.
list.quote: Build, design and innovate with the skills needed to solve real-world engineering challenges.

highlights.title: Engineering Science
highlights.desc: Maths, physics, mechanics and engineering drawing

highlights.title: Workshops
highlights.desc: Hands-on workshop, CAD lab and mini design builds

highlights.title: Industry Visits
highlights.desc: Plant visits and talks by practising engineers

highlights.title: Project Pipeline
highlights.desc: Third and fourth year capstone with industry problem

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Engineering Science & Workshop
curriculum.content: Engineering mathematics, physics, chemistry, basic electrical, engineering graphics and workshop practice. Practicals include drawing sheets, fitting/welding shop and basic circuits.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Core Branch Subjects
curriculum.content: Strength of materials or digital electronics (branch wise), thermodynamics / data structures, manufacturing processes, and a design-and-build mini project in the lab.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Industrial Training
curriculum.content: Core departmental subjects, industrial training, elective in automation or renewable energy, and a team project reviewed by faculty.

curriculum.title: Year 4 – Capstone & Specialization
curriculum.content: Specialization electives, major project / internship, professional ethics, and placement training including technical interviews and GATE awareness.

list.eligibility_text: B.Tech is for students who completed 12th with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM). Admission follows merit and counselling as per institute policy.
list.career_text: Engineering graduates join manufacturing, construction, IT product, energy, automobile and consulting firms. Options include M.Tech, GATE, PSU exams and entrepreneurship in product design.

faqs.question: Is PCM compulsory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in 12th are required.

faqs.question: How long is the degree?
faqs.answer: 4 years full time, including industrial training and a major project.

faqs.question: Are there workshops?
faqs.answer: Yes. Workshop, CAD and departmental labs run from year one.

eligibility_points: 12th pass with PCM from a recognized board.
Minimum 50% aggregate in PCM (as applicable).
Entrance / merit rank as published in the admission brochure.
Medical fitness and document verification at admission.

list.title: Science
list.description: Discover, research and create a better tomorrow with science.
list.overview: The B.Sc. Science program builds a strong base in physics, chemistry, mathematics or life sciences (as per combination), laboratory methods and scientific reporting. You learn to experiment, record data and think analytically.
list.quote: Discover, experiment and create a better tomorrow with the power of science.

highlights.title: Core Sciences
highlights.desc: Physics, chemistry, maths or biology combinations

highlights.title: Lab Intensive
highlights.desc: Regular practicals, records and viva

highlights.title: Research Basics
highlights.desc: Scientific writing and small investigation projects

highlights.title: Further Study Path
highlights.desc: Ready for M.Sc., teaching and lab technician roles

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Core Sciences & Labs
curriculum.content: Core papers in chosen science combination, lab techniques, environmental science and communication. You maintain practical records and learn units, errors and graph plotting.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Instrumentation & Investigation
curriculum.content: Intermediate theory in each subject, instrumentation basics, statistics for science and a small group investigation. Field visit or industry lab visit may be included.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Dissertation & Seminar
curriculum.content: Advanced papers, elective, dissertation or review project, and seminar presentation. Career sessions cover M.Sc. entrance, lab jobs and teaching.

list.eligibility_text: B.Sc. Science is for students who completed 12th with PCM or PCB, depending on the subject combination they choose at admission.
list.career_text: Science graduates work as lab technicians, quality analysts, research assistants, tutors and in pharma or food testing labs. Many continue M.Sc., B.Ed., or professional diplomas in medical lab technology.

faqs.question: PCM or PCB — which is needed?
faqs.answer: It depends on the combination. PCM for physical sciences; PCB for life sciences.

faqs.question: How much lab work is there?
faqs.answer: Practicals run every semester with records, viva and internal assessment.

faqs.question: Can I do M.Sc. after this?
faqs.answer: Yes. The degree is designed as a pathway to postgraduate science.

eligibility_points: 12th pass with PCM or PCB from a recognized board.
Minimum 50% in science subjects.
Subject combination allotted as per seats and marks.
Counselling to finalise Physics / Chemistry / Maths / Bio mix.

list.title: Commerce
list.description: Build a solid foundation in finance, accounting and trade.
list.overview: B.Com focuses on accounting, taxation, business law, banking and financial reporting. You learn to pass journal entries, file basics of GST/income tax concepts, and read company accounts used in offices and CA firms.
list.quote: Master the language of business and open doors to finance, banking and entrepreneurship.

highlights.title: Accountancy Core
highlights.desc: Financial accounting, cost and management accounts

highlights.title: Tax & Law
highlights.desc: GST concepts, income tax basics and business law

highlights.title: CA Firm Exposure
highlights.desc: Workshops with practising CAs and accountants

highlights.title: Banking Skills
highlights.desc: Banking, insurance and Tally / Excel practice

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Financial Accounting Basics
curriculum.content: Financial accounting, business organisation, business economics and business mathematics. Practicals include ledger posting, trial balance and basic Excel for commerce.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Tax, Law & Cost Accounts
curriculum.content: Corporate accounting, cost accounting, business law, income tax basics and auditing introduction. You will complete a small accounts project using Tally or spreadsheet tools.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – GST, Banking & Articleship Prep
curriculum.content: Management accounting, GST overview, banking & insurance, elective in finance, and internship in a CA firm, bank or accounts department.

list.eligibility_text: B.Com is ideal after 12th Commerce. Science and arts students can also apply if they are ready to study accounts and business maths from the first semester.
list.career_text: Commerce graduates join accounts teams, banks, insurance, GST practitioner assistance, CA articleship and family business. Many pursue CA, CMA, CS, M.Com or MBA Finance.

faqs.question: I did not take Accountancy in 12th. Can I join?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to seats. Bridge support is given in year-one accounts.

faqs.question: Will I learn Tally?
faqs.answer: Yes. Computerised accounting practice is part of the lab / workshop plan.

faqs.question: Is CA coaching included?
faqs.answer: The degree supports CA foundation concepts; dedicated CA coaching is optional / external.

eligibility_points: 12th pass; Commerce stream preferred.
Minimum 50% aggregate (as per policy).
Accountancy in 12th is an advantage, not compulsory for all seats.
Merit list and counselling for final allotment.

list.title: Medical & Health Sciences
list.description: Prepare for a rewarding career in healthcare and save lives.
list.overview: B.Sc. Medical & Health Sciences introduces anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, public health and clinical support skills. You learn patient-care basics, lab safety and how hospitals and diagnostics centres work.
list.quote: Serve with knowledge, compassion and the skills to make a difference in peoples lives.

highlights.title: Pre-Clinical Base
highlights.desc: Anatomy, physiology and biochemistry

highlights.title: Clinical Exposure
highlights.desc: Hospital / lab visits and case observations

highlights.title: Patient Skills
highlights.desc: Communication, ethics and first-aid modules

highlights.title: Healthcare Jobs
highlights.desc: Path to technician, coordinator and further medical study

curriculum.title: Year 1 – Anatomy & Physiology
curriculum.content: Human anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, English for health professionals and first aid. Practicals include models, charts and basic clinical measurements.

curriculum.title: Year 2 – Pathology & Public Health
curriculum.content: Pathology basics, microbiology, pharmacology introduction, nutrition and public health. Supervised hospital or diagnostic lab observation is scheduled.

curriculum.title: Year 3 – Clinical Posting
curriculum.content: Health administration, imaging / lab electives as offered, community posting, internship and a case-based project on a public-health topic.

curriculum.title: Year 4 – Internship & Specialization
curriculum.content: Specialisation modules (as notified), extended clinical internship, professional ethics and placement support for hospitals and diagnostic chains.

list.eligibility_text: This program is for students who completed 12th with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB). It is suitable if you want a healthcare career other than MBBS, or a pathway to allied health roles.
list.career_text: Graduates work in hospitals, diagnostic labs, public health projects, medical coding, clinical research support and hospital administration. Further study includes M.Sc. allied health, MPH or specialised diplomas.

faqs.question: Is NEET required?
faqs.answer: NEET is not required for this B.Sc. allied health pathway. PCB in 12th is required.

faqs.question: Will I work in a hospital?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observation, posting and internship in clinical settings are part of the course.

faqs.question: What is the duration?
faqs.answer: 4 years full time including internship, as per program structure.

eligibility_points: 12th pass with PCB from a recognized board.
Minimum 50% in PCB subjects.
Medical fitness certificate at the time of joining.
Counselling and document verification including mark sheets.

list.title: Diploma Programs
list.description: Short-term programs with practical knowledge and skills.
list.overview: Professional Diploma programs are short, job-focused courses in areas such as computer applications, digital office skills, electrician basics or hospitality (as offered each batch). Teaching is practical, with workshops and a final skill test.
list.quote: Learn faster, skill smarter and start your career with focused professional training.

highlights.title: Skill Modules
highlights.desc: Only job-relevant papers, no long theory load

highlights.title: Daily Practice
highlights.desc: Workshop / computer lab every week

highlights.title: Trainer Support
highlights.desc: Small batches and extra practice hours

highlights.title: Job Ready
highlights.desc: Portfolio, certificate and local employer connect

curriculum.title: Term 1 – Tools & Workplace Basics
curriculum.content: Orientation, safety, core tool training (computers or trade tools), communication for workplace and a first graded assignment. You start a simple portfolio from week three.

curriculum.title: Term 2 – Applied Job Skills
curriculum.content: Advanced modules of the chosen diploma, live tasks, guest trainer session and an internal skill test. Weak areas are revised in extra lab hours.

curriculum.title: Term 3 – Project, Certificate & Placement
curriculum.content: Capstone practical project, viva, certificate assessment and placement / freelance guidance. A short on-job exposure may be arranged with local partners.

list.eligibility_text: Diplomas are open after 10th or 12th, depending on the specific trade. They are meant for students who want a shorter, skill-based route into work rather than a three-year degree.
list.career_text: Diploma holders join as technicians, office assistants, junior designers, electricians (after trade diploma), or continue into a degree through lateral entry where eligible. Many start freelance or family-trade work immediately.

faqs.question: Can I join after 10th?
faqs.answer: Yes, for notified trades. Computer and office diplomas may need 12th.

faqs.question: How long is the diploma?
faqs.answer: Typically 1 year, split into three practical terms.

faqs.question: Will I get a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes. A completion certificate is issued after project and assessment.

eligibility_points: 10th pass for selected trades; 12th pass for others as notified.
Age and fitness criteria as per trade (especially workshop diplomas).
No stream restriction for computer / office diplomas.
Direct admission subject to seats; counselling on trade choice.

teachers.subtitle: MEET OUR EDUCATORS
teachers.description: Learn from experienced and passionate educators who are dedicated to helping you achieve your goals.

list.name: Prof. Neha Sharma
list.description: Making science simple and exciting through real-world examples and interactive learning.
list.bio: Prof. Neha Sharma is a passionate educator with over 6 years of experience in teaching science at school and online platforms. She believes in making science simple, engaging, and practical for every learner. Her teaching style focuses on real-world examples, critical thinking, and interactive learning, helping students build strong conceptual clarity and confidence.

list.name: Rahul Mehta
list.description: Passionate about coding and technology, helping students build skills for the digital future.
list.bio: Rahul Mehta is a full-stack developer and coding mentor with 8 years in the industry. He teaches programming through real projects, clean code habits, and interview-ready problem solving so students can move from basics to job-ready skills with confidence.

list.name: Pooja Verma
list.description: Turning complex chemistry concepts into easy and interesting lessons for every learner.
list.bio: Pooja Verma simplifies organic, inorganic, and physical chemistry with visual models and lab-style walkthroughs. Her sessions help board and competitive exam students remember reactions, mechanisms, and numericals without rote learning.

list.name: Dr. Anil Kumar
list.description: Helping students build a strong foundation in mathematics with clear and practical approach.
list.bio: Dr. Anil Kumar has taught school and undergraduate mathematics for more than a decade. He breaks algebra, calculus, and statistics into step-by-step methods so students can solve exam papers with speed and accuracy.

list.name: Karan Singh
list.description: Exploring the wonders of physics through practical demonstrations and hands-on learning.
list.bio: Karan Singh connects mechanics, electricity, and optics to everyday life. His classes use experiments, diagrams, and numerical drills so students understand why formulas work, not only how to memorize them.

list.name: Sneha Iyer
list.description: Helping students improve their communication skills and express their ideas with confidence.
list.bio: Sneha Iyer coaches students in grammar, writing, and spoken English. She focuses on clear expression, exam writing skills, and confident presentation so learners can perform well in class and in interviews.

list.name: Aditya Rao
list.description: Teaching creative design skills to turn ideas into visually stunning realities.
list.bio: Aditya Rao is a design educator who teaches visual thinking, branding, and digital tools. Students learn how to build portfolios, critique work, and ship designs that look professional for clients and internships.

list.name: Meera Joshi
list.description: Inspiring curiosity about life sciences and making biology engaging for every student.
list.bio: Meera Joshi makes cell biology, genetics, and human physiology easy to visualize. Her lessons mix diagrams, mnemonics, and exam-style questions so students stay curious and exam-ready at the same time.
